newsitem.title: USA: American Exp plans 140 wells for rest of year.
newsitem.headline: American Exp plans 140 wells for rest of year.

text.p: American Exploration Co plans to drill 140 wells for the remainder of 1997 after drilling 13 in the first quarter, of which 11 were successful, the company said in a statement with earnings.

This program will include development drilling on existing properties as well as significant exploration wells in South Texas, the Cotton Valley Pinnacle Reef Trend and the Gulf of Mexico, several of which will be drilled in the second quarter, the company said on Tuesday.
Exploration and development expenditures during the first quarter of 1997 were $22 million.

Revenues in the first quarter rose to $24.7 million in the first quarter of 1997 from $16.6 million a year ago cash flow before working capital and after preferred dividends more than doubled to $15.1 million, $0.97 per share, from $6.7 million, $0.57 a share.
Production averaged 76,573 thousand cubic feet of natural gas (mcf) and 4,428 barrels of oil per day (bpd) compared to 50,546 mcf of gas and 4,862 bpd of oil.
Average natgas prices rose to $2.56 per mcf from $1.86 and crude rose to $18.59 per barrel from $16.58.
"Higher realized natural gas prices were primarily due to lower levels of hedging in the first quarter of 1997 compared to the first quarter of 1996," the company said.

American said that production and operating expenses fell to $4.20 per barrel of energy equivalent produced from $5.04 per barrel of oil equivalent BOE due to lower cost production, primarily in the Gulf of Mexico.
Barrels of oil equivalent are calculated by dividing billions of cubic feet of natural gas by six and adding it to million barrels of crude and natural gas liquids.
General and administrative expenses rose in overall terms, to $2.2 million from $1.8 million, although they fell per barrel of production to $1.40 per BOE from $1.52.
